newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAA says little impact from one-day strike.
newsitem.headline: SAA says little impact from one-day strike.

text.p: State-run South African Airways (SAA) said on Monday there had been little disruption from a one-day general strike to protest new labour legislation.
"Domestic flight are coming in as normal and there have been no major disruptions," SAS spokesman Mike Pheiffer told Reuters.
But he said the situation would have to be reviewed later.
"So far nothing has been affected but it is still too early to say what the situation will be like tonight with international flight going out," he said.

South Africa's biggest labour federation, the 1.9 million strong Congress of South African Trade Unions, has mobilised its members to protest against the Basic Conditions of Employment Bill which has already passed through Cabinet.
Cosatu is demanding a 40 hour working week, six months maternity leave, double pay for Sunday work and the minimum age for formal employment to be set at 18 years.
